title: NLTK FramenetCorpusReader -- T1005 caller-supplied frame name reaches builtin open(), same pathsec-bypass class as NKJPCorpusReader
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-12074 (GHSA-xh95-f55m-82fw,
CVSS 7.5 HIGH), affecting NLTK's `FramenetCorpusReader.frame()`.

`frame_by_name` builds an XML file path by joining the corpus root,
the frame directory, and a caller-supplied frame name with a fixed
`.xml` extension -- no containment check -- then constructs an
`XMLCorpusView` from that STRING path rather than a `PathPointer`.
Because the view is built from a string, it reads with the builtin
`open()`, so `nltk.pathsec.validate_path()` is never invoked and
`ENFORCE = True` does not block a `../` sequence in the name. This is
the same builtin-open-bypasses-the-sandbox class as this corpus's
sibling `NKJPCorpusReader` rule (CVE-2026-12072), but in a distinct
reader class and code path: `frame_by_name` never goes through
`CorpusReader.open()` at all, so that reader's protection does not
extend to it. The same string-path pattern additionally exists in
`doc()` (using an index-entry `filename` field) and the lexical-unit
file loader (using a `lexUnit` ID attribute), both reachable through
a malicious or attacker-modified FrameNet corpus index rather than a
direct caller argument.

Detection logic flags a `FramenetCorpusReader.frame()` invocation
whose frame-name argument contains a `../` path-traversal sequence --
the exact escape this advisory's proof of concept uses, with
`nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE = True` set before import, to read a
secret-marked frame XML file planted outside a minimal valid FrameNet
corpus root.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (nltk, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact function, the string-vs-PathPointer
distinction, the two sibling reachable code paths, and a runnable
proof of concept with `ENFORCE = True` explicitly enabled), fixed in NLTK 3.10.0 (PR #3581, verified via live GitHub changelog lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
